reuse.why: Merges the three identical category queries of the average actions into one getBudgetableCategories and reuses getBudgetData's existing hidden columns in copyPreviousMonth; there was no existing template predicate to reuse.

duplication.why: Removes three query copies, but the exclusion rule (hidden, group hidden, saved template) is written twice: as SQL in getBudgetableCategories and as a JS condition in copyPreviousMonth.

placement.why: The selection lives in budget/actions.ts beside getBudgetData, where the month-wide actions and their category queries already are.

scope.why: Only the month-wide actions, the shared query and a focused test change.

maintainability.why: A future change to which categories month-wide actions skip must be made in two different forms (SQL WHERE and a JS if), and the copy test only covers the averages.

bypasses_abstraction.where: copyPreviousMonth applies the rule with its own inline condition on getBudgetData rows instead of the new getBudgetableCategories selection.

disguised_duplication.where: The template test appears as `c.goal_def IS NULL OR c.goal_def = '[]'` in getBudgetableCategories and as its negation `goal_def != null && goal_def !== '[]'` in copyPreviousMonth, alongside a second hidden/group-hidden check.

one_place.where: setZero and the 3/6/12-month averages use getBudgetableCategories, but copyPreviousMonth decides the same rule separately in JS.
